content: Phase 40 plan: Roadmap as a DAG (3.4.0). See docs/phases/roadmap-dag.md. Optional '- **Depends on:** …' line per roadmap phase (slug / Phase N / exact name; unknown/self/cycle are errors listed by 'roadmap check'); stable-Kahn topological 'roadmap queue' (edge-free roadmaps byte-identical to 3.3.0); 'roadmap graph [--mermaid]', 'roadmap ready [--json]', 'roadmap phases' gains a depends_on column only when present; full-roadmap advance picks the next READY queue entry (re-parses roadmap), never starts a blocked phase — sets roadmap.pause_reason + turn:lead command, 'roadmap resume' re-runs the advance; new tagteam/worktree.py: 'roadmap worktree <phase> [--from REF] [--remove [--force]]' creates ../<repo>-<phase> on branch phase-<slug>, seeds framework files, registers it as an ordinary project (registry format unchanged; metadata in ~/.tagteam/worktrees.json), prints kickoff; 'roadmap worktrees [--json]' lists path/branch/phase/state/merged; refuses not-ready/unknown/duplicate; --remove refuses unmerged without --force. Two worktrees = two projects (independent state, watcher, gate, panel). Out: two phases in one root, auto-merge, cockpit UI. Tests: parsing/validation/topo (diamond, ties, start semantics), watcher blocked/resume, worktree create/list/remove in temp git repos, flag-off byte-identical, SKILL copies identical. Open questions: sibling dir vs .worktrees/; 'roadmap resume' vs 'tagteam resume'; require ready vs not-terminal for worktree creation.

The overall direction is sound, and I agree with the proposed answers to the open questions: use sibling worktrees, keep `roadmap resume` separate from the existing dispatch resume, and require graph readiness before worktree creation. Please revise the plan to close these correctness gaps before implementation:

1. Define one authoritative dependency-satisfaction rule across commands and the watcher. Today an impl APPROVE only adds the phase to `state["roadmap"]["completed"]`; it does not make that phase terminal in `docs/roadmap.md`. As written, re-parsing the roadmap after an approval can therefore leave every dependent blocked forever. Specify how `ready`, full-roadmap advance, and worktree creation combine persisted roadmap dispositions with the active run's completed list. Also specify the cross-worktree publication contract: e.g. the phase branch must commit a terminal roadmap disposition and that commit must be merged before another project can observe it. Add tests for both same-run approval unblocking a dependent without a manual roadmap edit and merged cross-worktree completion unblocking it.

2. Resolve the contradiction in `queue [start]`. The plan says nonterminal predecessors are “assumed done,” while also promising that full-roadmap mode never starts a blocked phase. A requested start whose dependency is nonterminal cannot silently bypass that edge. Prefer either including every nonterminal dependency ancestor before the requested phase, or rejecting the start with the blockers; retain the old suffix behavior only for edge-free roadmaps. Pin the chosen behavior in CLI and watcher tests.

3. Make dynamic advancement explicit. A stored topological queue can become stale when another worktree finishes and merges a queued phase. On every impl advance/resume, skip entries that are already terminal or recorded complete, advance `current_index` to the phase actually selected, and produce `roadmap-complete` when no incomplete entries remain. Add the parallel diamond case where a middle queue entry completes externally before the main watcher reaches it.

4. Validate graph identities before building the slug-keyed dict. Duplicate phase numbers and duplicate normalized slugs (including different names that slugify identically) make references ambiguous and currently risk silent dict overwrite / branch collision. `roadmap check`, `queue`, `ready`, and worktree creation should fail with all such identity errors; add tests.

5. Define the worktree merge target used by `merged?` and safe removal. Record the parent/integration branch (and base ref when `--from` is used) at creation, then check whether the phase branch is merged into that recorded target rather than whichever branch happens to be checked out later. Test parent branch switching before list/remove.

Round 2 — all five points addressed in docs/phases/roadmap-dag.md (Design → "One dependency-satisfaction rule", "Full-roadmap mode", "Worktrees"; Scope A/B/E; Success criteria 2–5; open questions moved to "Decisions" as agreed: sibling dir, separate `roadmap resume`, require ready).

1. One rule: `satisfied(dep) := is_terminal_status(roadmap disposition on disk) OR normalize_phase_key(dep) in state.roadmap.completed (active run)`. Used identically by `roadmap ready` (reads the project's handoff-state when run_mode=full-roadmap, prints "(+ N completed in the active run)", `--roadmap-only` ignores it), the watcher advance/`roadmap resume`, and `roadmap worktree`. So an impl APPROVE that only appends to `completed` (unchanged behaviour) unblocks dependents in the same run — tested. Cross-worktree publication contract spelled out: another project observes completion only through docs/roadmap.md in its own checked-out tree → phase branch commits a terminal `Status:` disposition and is merged into the recorded target; siblings see it after merging/rebasing that branch; until then dependents stay blocked there by design. Tests: same-run unblocking without a roadmap edit; temp repo worktree commits terminal status → merged → parent's `ready` unblocks (and not before).

2. `queue [start]` no longer "assumes done": the queue = {start} ∪ incomplete phases after start ∪ every nonterminal, not-completed dependency ancestor of those (transitively), topologically ordered — unmet ancestors are pulled in AHEAD of start and reported on stderr; unneeded predecessors are dropped as today; edge-free roadmaps → today's suffix byte-identical. Pinned in CLI tests and a watcher `--roadmap [start]` test.

3. Dynamic advance made explicit as five steps on every advance/resume: re-parse (invalid → pause "roadmap invalid: …"); walk queue[current_index+1:] skipping entries terminal on disk or in `completed` (logged, not started, `completed` stays "approved in this run"); select the first entry whose deps are satisfied and set current_index = THAT index; no incomplete entry left → roadmap-complete; incomplete but all blocked → pause_reason "blocked: <phase> depends on <deps>", turn:lead, no start; `roadmap resume` re-runs the same function through update_state(expected_seq). Tests: diamond A→{B,C}→D with B completed externally while on A → skip B, select C (index 2), then D; all-blocked → pause + resume; externally-completed tail → roadmap-complete.

4. `validate_identities(phases)` runs before any slug-keyed dict: duplicate heading numbers, duplicate normalized slugs (different names slugifying identically), empty names — all problems listed in one RoadmapGraphError; refused by check/queue/ready/graph/worktree creation, and the advance pauses on it. Applies to edge-free roadmaps too (a duplicate slug was already a latent bug), so the byte-identical guarantee is stated for well-formed edge-free roadmaps — this repo's 40-phase roadmap and all fixtures qualify (verified: no duplicate numbers/slugs; a test asserts it). `parse_roadmap` itself stays lenient so `roadmap phases` output is unchanged.

5. Sidecar records `target` (parent's checked-out branch at creation, or `--target BRANCH`) and `base` (resolved sha of HEAD/`--from`). `merged?` = `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> <target>` in the parent repo against refs/heads/<target>, falling back to origin/<target> if the local branch is gone (squash-merge + local delete); neither → "target missing" = unmerged. `--remove` refuses unmerged/missing-target without `--force`. Test switches the parent to another branch between creation and list/remove.
